The pond stores the tide between one turning and the next, and the wheel waits until the head is enough to move the stone. Millers wrote the hours down because the sea does not keep a clock, and a formula was how they said what the water would do. Families who lived beside the pond learned to read the marks cut into the wall the way other people read a timetable.
